Theme

Work & responsibility · Money, work & business

trade noun

a craft, a skilled occupation

also craft, handicraft, by trade, learn a trade, the trades, skilled trade

classical

Cic. Off. 1.150 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 161: exercēre ūnum ex artificiīs, to practise one of the trades
Traupman 165, 397
Traupman 298

artificium, artificiī n.

noun, second declension

a trade, a craft

The occupation of a craftsman (Lewis & Short); Traupman’s word for a trade.

Other words

  • ars, artis f. — a skill; the craft or profession one lives by

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Ov. Met. 3.588: ars illī sua cēnsus erat; M-O s.v. work, job: career, profession

    In Cicero both the crafts and the learned professions (Off. 1.150–151).

  • quaestus, quaestūs m. — a living, a way of making money

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. work, job: quō quaestū tē tenēs?, what do you do for a living?; Traupman 309

    For the trade as a living rather than a skill; Cicero pairs it with artificium (Off. 1.150).

Examples

  • ars illī sua cēnsus erat

    his trade was all his wealthOv. Met. 3.588

  • litterae thēsaurum est, et artificium nunquam moritur

    learning is a treasure, and a trade never dies (a freedman speaking)Petr. 46

See also job, professional, career, industry.
